title: Vice-President inaugurates New Super Specialty Block of Holy Family Hospital in New Delhi
subtitle:
Vice-President calls for collaborative national efforts to strengthen cancer care and research
Benefits of medical research must reach all humanity, not remain confined to a few: Vice-President
Healthcare institutions must combine medical excellence with compassion and affordability: Vice-President
Healthy India is the foundation of Viksit Bharat@2047: Vice-President
body_text:
The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today inaugurated the New Super Specialty Block of Holy Family Hospital at Okhla, New Delhi. He also released the Holy Family Hospital Souvenir 2026 and felicitated individuals associated with the construction of the new block. Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurated the New Super Specialty Block of Holy Family Hospital in New Delhi today, marking an important step towards expanding access to specialised healthcare.

Highlighting the need for collaborative efforts in cancer care and research, he emphasised that medical advancements must benefit all sections of society. — Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) November 27, 2026 Recalling the hospital’s historical legacy, the Vice-President noted that its foundation stone was laid in 1953 by the then Vice-President of India, Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan. He said that the continuity of this legacy reflects how institutions founded with noble intentions continue to serve society across generations. Appreciating the hospital’s commitment to providing healthcare irrespective of caste, creed, religion or economic status, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that the philosophy of India’s civilisational ethos rests on mutual respect and the freedom of every individual to practise their faith. He observed that good initiatives and selfless service must always be encouraged and celebrated. Highlighting the importance of collaborative efforts in combating cancer, the Vice-President called for creating a common forum bringing together cancer treatment institutions across the country to share research, knowledge and best practices. He emphasised that the benefits of medical research and innovation must reach all sections of humanity and should not remain confined to a few countries or privileged sections. He expressed his willingness to take initiatives towards strengthening such collaboration. The Vice-President said that the new Super Specialty Block would expand access to specialised healthcare. He observed that the success of such facilities would ultimately depend on their ability to combine advanced medical treatment with affordability, compassion and a human touch. Referring to the Government’s efforts under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Vice-President highlighted the expansion of India’s healthcare infrastructure. He noted that initiatives such as Ayushman Bharat and PM Jan Arogya Yojana have helped reduce the financial burden of hospitalisation on economically weaker families. He also highlighted the significant increase in AIIMS institutions, medical colleges and MBBS and postgraduate medical seats over the past decade, bringing specialised healthcare and medical education closer to people across the country. Emphasising that the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047 must ensure that the benefits of development reach every citizen, including those in villages and smaller towns, he said that charitable hospitals and voluntary organisations are important partners in strengthening India’s healthcare ecosystem. Stressing that infrastructure and advanced equipment alone cannot define a hospital’s strength, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that its real strength lies in the dedication, expertise and human touch of its healthcare professionals. He observed that a healthy society is indispensable for building a developed nation and called for collective efforts towards sustainable and inclusive development. Reverend Andrea Francia, Chargé d’Affaires, Apostolic Nunciature in India; Reverend Archbishop Anil J. T. Couto, President, New Delhi Holy Family Hospital Society; Reverend Deepak Valerian Tauro, Auxiliary Bishop of the Archdiocese of Delhi; Father George P. A., Director, Holy Family Hospital, and other dignitaries were present on the occasion **** PR/ASM/VMJ
